purpose: Capivasertib is used to treat a certain type of breast cancer called HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer. It is used together with another medicine called fulvestrant. It is specifically for adults whose cancer has a certain genetic change (mutation) in the PIK3CA, AKT1, or PTEN genes.
how_it_works: Cancer cells sometimes have faulty signals that tell them to keep growing out of control. Capivasertib works by blocking a specific protein called AKT, which is like a switch that cancer cells use to grow and survive. By turning off that switch, this medicine helps slow down or stop the cancer from spreading.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, rash or skin changes (including a rash that looks like acne), nausea, tiredness, mouth sores, vomiting, high blood sugar levels, decreased appetite, urinary tract infections, and dry or itchy skin. Most side effects can be managed, so let your care team know if anything bothers you.
warnings: This medicine can cause high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), which may be serious — your blood sugar will need to be monitored regularly. It can also cause serious skin reactions, so report any severe rash right away. Capivasertib can harm an unborn baby, so do not become pregnant while taking it and use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after. It may also affect male fertility. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as some drugs can interact with capivasertib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 400 mg (two 200 mg tablets) taken by mouth twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening — for 4 days in a row, followed by 3 days off. This means you take it Tuesday through Friday, then skip Saturday, Sunday, and Monday, for example. You can take it with or without food. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
